correctness.rationale: The induction is valid for every \(m\ge0\). For arbitrary \(k\), a fresh prime \(p\nmid abk\) makes \(\tau(akp^{r-1})=r\tau(ak)\) and \(\tau(bkp^{r-1})=r\tau(bk)\) for every \(r\ge1\). The induction hypothesis then applies exactly to the definition of quasi-injectivity and yields \(\tau(ak)=\tau(bk)\); published quasi-injectivity of \(\tau\) gives \(a=b\). The Jordan corollary follows from the published all-order quasi-injectivity of \(J_s\).
